title: STRANGE MINUTE · WHAT IF #11

lines.text: What if you stepped onto Mars without a spacesuit?
First problem: the air is 95% carbon dioxide.
lines.say: First problem: the air is ninety-five percent carbon dioxide.

lines.text: And there's almost none of it. Under 1% of Earth's pressure.
lines.say: And there's almost none of it. Under one percent of Earth's pressure.

lines.text: The air in your lungs would rush straight out.
Your saliva would start to boil. At body temperature.
In 1966, a NASA tester's suit leaked in a vacuum chamber.
lines.say: In nineteen sixty-six, a NASA tester's suit leaked in a vacuum chamber.

lines.text: He felt the spit bubbling on his tongue. Then he blacked out.
Your skin would swell up. But you would not explode.
It's freezing too: about minus 80 degrees on average.
lines.say: It's freezing too: about minus eighty degrees on average.

lines.text: And there's no ozone layer, so raw sunlight burns.
The one fun part? Gravity is just 38% of Earth's.
lines.say: The one fun part? Gravity is just thirty-eight percent of Earth's.

lines.text: You could jump almost three times higher. Once.
Within two minutes, it's over. Would you still take one step?
lines.say: Within two minutes, it's over. Would you still take one step?

sources: NASA Mars facts: atmosphere ~95% CO2, surface pressure ~0.6% of Earth's, gravity ~38%, average temp about -80 F (-60 C), no ozone layer
NASA 1966 Jim LeBlanc vacuum chamber suit leak: conscious ~12-15 s, felt saliva boiling on tongue, survived
Ebullition at body temperature below Armstrong limit (~6.3 kPa); Mars ~0.6 kPa; survival ~1-2 min (vacuum exposure studies)
